findings.parent_candidate: domain:natural-sciences (via LCC GE filing under class G — opposes)
findings.claim: LCC assigns Environmental sciences to GE1–GE350, which is a member of class G (Geography. Anthropology. Recreation), not class Q (Science). The full compound label is 'Geography. Anthropology. Recreation--Environmental sciences'.

UDC class 5 (MATHEMATICS. NATURAL SCIENCES) directly contains 502/504 'Environmental science. Conservation of natural resources. Threats to the environment and protection against them', placing environmental science inside the natural sciences top-level class.
findings.quote: 5 MATHEMATICS. NATURAL SCIENCES ... 502/504 Environmental science. Conservation of natural resources. Threats to the environment and protection against them

findings.claim: The OECD Fields of Research and Development (FORD) taxonomy, hosted by the Slovenian Research and Innovation Agency (ARIS), lists '1.5. Earth and related Environmental sciences' as a sub-field directly under '1. Natural Sciences', co-equal with Mathematics, Physical sciences, Chemical sciences, and Biological sciences.
findings.quote: 1. Natural Sciences 1.1. Mathematics 1.2. Computer and information sciences 1.3. Physical sciences 1.4. Chemical sciences 1.5. Earth and related Environmental sciences 1.6. Biological sciences 1.7. Other natural sciences

findings.claim: Britannica defines environmental science as an 'interdisciplinary academic field that draws on ecology, geology, meteorology, biology, chemistry, engineering, and physics', explicitly framing it as bridging multiple sciences. The editorial breadcrumb places it under 'Science > Environment', not under a single natural-science parent. It explicitly distinguishes environmental science (quantitative, natural science methods) from environmental studies (social/political focus).
findings.quote: interdisciplinary academic field that draws on ecology , geology , meteorology , biology , chemistry , engineering , and physics to study environmental problems and human impacts on the environment

findings.claim: Nature Portfolio's subject page for environmental sciences defines it as 'the multidisciplinary study of all aspects of the Earth's physical and biological environments', encompassing environmental chemistry, soil science, ecology, climatology, marine and freshwater systems, and agriculture. No single-parent subject breadcrumb beyond 'nature > subjects' is assigned.
findings.quote: Environmental science is the multidisciplinary study of all aspects of the Earth's physical and biological environments. It encompasses environmental chemistry, soil science, ecology, climatology, vegetation cover, marine and freshwater systems, as well as environmental remediation and preservation, and agriculture and land use.

findings.parent_candidate: non-natural-sciences home (NCES CIP 03 — Natural Resources and Conservation framing — context)
findings.claim: The US National Center for Education Statistics CIP (Classification of Instructional Programs) places Environmental Science (03.0104) under CIP family 03 'Natural Resources and Conservation', not under a pure-sciences family. The definition explicitly uses natural-science methods: 'focuses on the application of biological, chemical, and physical principles to the study of the physical environment'.
findings.quote: A program that focuses on the application of biological, chemical, and physical principles to the study of the physical environment and the solution of environmental problems, including subjects such as abating or controlling environmental pollution and degradation; the interaction between human society and the natural environment; and natural resources management. Includes instruction in biology, chemistry, physics, geosciences, climatology, statistics, and mathematical modeling.

findings.parent_candidate: institutional housing — interdisciplinary / Natural Resources college framing
findings.claim: UC Berkeley's Department of Environmental Science, Policy, and Management (ESPM) sits within the Rausser College of Natural Resources and describes itself as 'a multidisciplinary program'. This is institutionally distinct from both a standalone natural-science school and a liberal-arts placement.
findings.quote: The Department of Environmental Science, Policy, and Management is a multidisciplinary program that recognizes the urgency of the challenges, and the enormous opportunities that may lead to transformative change.

notes:
SPLIT ACROSS CLASSIFICATION SYSTEMS — core finding: LCC and UDC/FORD directly conflict. LCC places environmental sciences in class G (Geography/Anthropology/Recreation), outside the Q science classes, which is a hard 'opposes' for domain:natural-sciences. By contrast, UDC (class 5) and OECD FORD (section 1) both file it unambiguously within natural sciences at the same structural level as chemistry, biology, and physics. The FORD evidence is especially strong as it is the primary international research classification used by UNESCO, EU Horizon, and national science agencies; it was last revised in Frascati Manual 2015.

FIELD-LEVEL QUESTION: FORD's 1.5 'Earth and related Environmental sciences' is parallel in structure to 1.3 Physical sciences and 1.6 Biological sciences — all are listed as numerically co-equal sub-fields of Natural Sciences. This supports field-level status within domain:natural-sciences, not a sub-sub-field. UDC similarly places 502/504 as a direct child of class 5, at the same depth as 51 (Mathematics) or 59 (Zoology). CIP places it under 'Natural Resources and Conservation' (03), which is an applied/management framing distinct from pure-science — this is a third classification philosophy and is recorded as context, not a vote for or against natural sciences. Institutional patterns are mixed: Berkeley ESPM is in a Natural Resources college (applied), UVA Environmental Sciences is in Arts & Sciences (umbrella), Yale and Stanford operate as standalone environment/sustainability schools. None of the institutional patterns constitutes a clean 'this is natural sciences' placement.

INTERDISCIPLINARITY vs. PARENT: Britannica and Nature both explicitly call it 'interdisciplinary' or 'multidisciplinary' without assigning a single parent domain — these are correctly coded as 'interface'. The orchestrator should apply the two-reading robustness test: the UDC + FORD reading strongly supports domain:natural-sciences; the LCC reading opposes it; the section-13 dual-membership option could be explored given the LCC split. The field-level modeling (vs. sub-field of earth science) appears reasonable given FORD's treatment: 1.5 is not subordinate to another FORD field, it is co-equal.

ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCE vs. ENVIRONMENTAL STUDIES: Britannica explicitly notes environmental science is quantitative and distinct from environmental studies (social/political). NCES CIP has only one code in 03.01 for environmental science (03.0104); no separate environmental studies code exists in the 03.01 group. This sourced distinction confirms the node represents the science sub-discipline, not the humanities/social-science variant.
